description.p: A stopwatch that never loses time. Instead of counting ticks, it stores the moment you pressed start, so closing the app, suspending the machine, or rebooting does not stop the clock. Reopen it days later and the elapsed time is exactly right.

ul.li: Elapsed time survives application restarts and system reboots
Lap times with per-lap splits and running totals, fastest and slowest highlighted
Keyboard shortcuts: Space to start and pause, L for lap, R to reset
Native Plasma look and feel, built with Kirigami
Works from the command line too: start, pause, lap, reset and print the status without opening a window

description.p: Command line control and a few quality of life changes:

ul.li: New options --start, --pause, --lap, --reset, --status and --laps, which work without opening a window
Only one window at a time; launching again raises it
Shows when the current run was started
Start, pause, lap and reset from the launcher's context menu
Man page and bash, zsh and fish completions

description.p: First release: start, pause, reset and laps, kept across restarts and reboots.
